annotations.title: Ask to submit for App Review

description: Asks a person to approve submitting an iOS build that is on TestFlight for App Review; the in-app products that are ready to submit go to review with it. When the version is already with App Review with an older build, this is refused and says so; replace: true then asks for both steps under one approval: Ploa withdraws the version from App Review, puts this build on it and submits it (App Review starts over). When App Review rejected the version, this sends it back, with this build (a newer one or the same): Ploa puts it on the version and resubmits the submission App Review sent back, as App Store Connect's Resubmit to App Review does, so never do that by hand there; if App Review rejected something else in that submission too (an in-app event, a product page), it says so, and the person fixes or removes it in App Store Connect first. It never waits for a reply to App Review: a rejection that asked for a fix goes back without any text (the fix is the answer), and when App Review's message asks for an answer, the request says so before the person approves, as the thread closes once the version goes back. With replyId (a reply to App Review's message drafted with ploa_app_review_reply), Ploa first puts that reply in the version's App Review Information › Notes, under the same approval, so App Review reads it with the resubmission. Nothing is sent to Apple until a person approves on the Ploa dashboard; this returns at once with the request's ID, so check it with ploa_approval_status. Needs a token allowed to submit.

releaseId.description: The release ID that ploa_release_start returned.

replace.description: The version is with App Review with another build: withdraw it and submit this build in its place, under one approval.

replyId.description: A reply to App Review's message for this version, from ploa_app_review_reply: Ploa puts it in the version's App Review notes before submitting.
